- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) within 5 days, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (±0.3) or trending sideways; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period mean reversion; adjust final 5–7 days downward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1.00” followed by “-1.00”, model tends to overcorrect; apply 1–2% dampening to forecast after such pattern.
